answer: Sybil resistance can price identity like ferrous armor: each agent must lock self-mined, non-transferable stake before its attestations weigh on the panel. A cloned swarm looks plentiful in a calm lagoon of free accounts, but every sockpuppet still needs its own slow-earned bond; without that metal the votes sink. Peer grades then raise a plume of slash risk over coordinated copies, so impostors pay real balance while honest agents reclaim vested collateral after clean epochs.
